## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
```{r}
#############################################################
# Using the sf package
library(sp) # for meuse data
library(sf)
data(meuse)
```

```{r}
# meuse_crs <- "+init=epsg:28992"
meuse <- st_as_sf(meuse, coords=c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs("EPSG:28992"))
st_crs(meuse)
rm(meuse)
data(meuse)
class(meuse)
meuse <- st_as_sf(meuse, coords=c("x", "y"))
st_crs(meuse)
meuse <- st_set_crs(meuse, st_crs("EPSG:28992"))
# sometimes data does not have a spatial component - that is why you set the CRS 
st_crs(meuse)
summary(meuse) # these are data.frames!
names(meuse)
plot(meuse)
plot(meuse["zinc"]) # make a plot of just zinc
```


```{r}
# the geometry - the geometry is what makes the spatial data an sf object
st_geometry(meuse)
st_crs(meuse)
# st_set_crs(meuse) <- "4326" # Doesn't reproject - does not reproject the points 
# reprojecting the data so that all the data is in the same projection 
meuse_wgs84 <- st_transform(meuse, st_crs("EPSG:4326")) # project to WGS84, EPSG:4326
# makes the points actually lat long data 
st_geometry(meuse_wgs84)
```
```{r}
#############################################################
# now lets read in an ESRI shapefile
nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package="sf"))
nc[order(nc$AREA, decreasing=TRUE), c("AREA", "NAME")]
st_geometry(nc)
names(nc)
```
```{r}
# let's map the SIDs incidence - SID is sudden infant death syndome - just raw numbers, not a porportion
plot(nc["SID79"])
```
```{r}
# create a new column for SID rate
nc$SID79r <- nc$SID79 / nc$BIR79
plot(nc[c("SID79", "SID79r")])
```
```{r}
library(viridis)
plot(nc["SID79r"], pal=inferno, breaks=c(0,0.003))
qs <- quantile(as.numeric(unlist(nc$SID79r)), c(0, 0.02, 0.98, 1))
breaks <- c(qs[1], seq(qs[2], qs[3], len)
```

```{r}
library(RColorBrewer)
display.brewer.all()
mybrewerpal <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "Blues"))
plot(nc["SID79r"], breaks="fisher", pal=mybrewerpal)
```
```{r}
#############################################################

# Solutions to lecture challenge
# 1) Which NC county has highest area?
nc[order(nc$AREA, decreasing=TRUE), "NAME"][1,] # by sorting
nc[which.max(nc$AREA), "NAME"] # with filtering
```
```{r}
# 2) What is the FIPS code for Wake County
nc[nc$NAME == "Wake", "FIPS"]
```
```{r}
# 3) Make a map of NC counties colorized by FIPS code
plot(nc["FIPS"]) # FIPS is character and so treated as a factor, so we get discrete colors
# compare to numeric:
nc$FIPSnum <- as.numeric(nc$FIPS)
plot(nc["FIPSnum"]) # now we get a continuous color ramp
```
```{r}
# 4) Create a simple feature collection of 1000 random points...
n <- 1000
knids <- data.frame(x=runif(n, 0, 360), y=runif(n, 0, 90), elev=rnorm(n, 100, 25), soil=sample(LETTERS[1:3], n, rep=T), foundknid=sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), n, rep=T))
knids <- st_as_sf(knids, coords=c("x", "y"), crs=st_crs("EPSG:4326"))
plot(knids)
```

```{r}
#############################################################

library(raster)
library(viridis)
```
path_to_data <- "/Users/jmgray2/Google Drive/My Drive/Teaching/GIS713/GDM_RCodeData"
setwd(path_to_data)

r <- raster("kansas_sub")
class(r)
projection(r)
ncell(r)
xres(r)
extent(r)
plot(r)
click(r)
click(r, cell=T, xy=T, type="p")
zoom(r)
v <- values(r) # extract values to a data.frame

s <- stack("kansas_sub")
nlayers(s)
v <- values(s)
dim(v)
head(v)
plot(s)
plot(s, 4)
plotRGB(s, 4, 3, 2)
plotRGB(s, 4, 3, 2, stretch="lin")
?plotRGB

qs <- quantile(raster(s, 4), c(0, 0.02, 0.98, 1))
breaks <- unique(c(qs[1], seq(qs[2], qs[3], len=254), qs[4]))
pal <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral")))
plot(raster(s, 4), breaks=breaks, col=pal(length(breaks) - 1))

# or, using viridis
plot(raster(s, 4), breaks=breaks, col=plasma(length(breaks) - 1))

# creating new rasters
r <- raster(matrix(rnorm(100), nrow=10, ncol=10))
plot(r)
# various ways to set the values
r[] <- 10 # using bracket style
r <- setValues(r, rnorm(100, mean=10, sd=0.2)) # using the setValues function
r[sample(1:ncell(r), 10)] <- NA # using particular cell numbers
plot(r, colNA="black")
r[1,] <- 10 # set an entire row
values(r) <- 1:ncell(r) # using the values function; fills by row

# extracting values via points using sampleRandom
r_samp <- sampleRandom(r, 10, sp=T)
r_samp@data
spplot(r_samp)
plot(r)
plot(r_samp, add=T)

# or, from some other dataset
set.seed(42)
r <- raster("kansas_sub", 4)
cdl <- raster("kansas_sub_2011_CDL.tif")
plot(cdl)

# create a random sample as a SpatialPointsDataFrame
num_samples <- 100
x_samp <- sample(xmin(r):xmax(r), num_samples, rep=T)
y_samp <- sample(ymin(r):ymax(r), num_samples, rep=T)
samp_df <- data.frame(x=x_samp, y=y_samp, index=1:num_samples)
coordinates(samp_df) <- ~ x + y
plot(r)
plot(samp_df, add=T, pch=1, col="black")

# extract the Landsat NIR values and the CDL codes at sample points
samp_df$nir <- extract(r, samp_df)
samp_df$cdl <- extract(cdl, samp_df)
head(samp_df)
boxplot(nir~cdl, data=samp_df)

# get the colors from the CDL color table, and boxplot with proper colors
boxplot(nir~cdl, data=samp_df, col=colortable(cdl)[sort(unique(samp_df$cdl)) + 1])

# extract values using a polygon
r_qs <- quantile(r, c(0, 0.02, 0.98, 1))
breaks <- c(r_qs[1], seq(r_qs[2], r_qs[3], len=254), r_qs[4])
plot(r, breaks=breaks, col=viridis(255))

samp_poly <- drawPoly()
poly_extract <- extract(r, samp_poly)
class(poly_extract)
# names(poly_extract)
length(poly_extract[[1]])
hist(poly_extract[[1]])
extract(r, samp_poly, fun=mean)
extract(r, samp_poly, fun=range)
myf <- function(x, na.rm=T) median(x, na.rm=na.rm) - mean(x, na.rm=na.rm)
extract(r, samp_poly, fun=myf)
